title: The Orchard of the Palatinate
premise: In 1908, Hazel Ravensworth, a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Meridian Trading Company in the Palatinate river ports, believes history belongs to other people — until a sealed letter implicates her family in a conspiracy to smuggle a deposed archduke's heir out of the empire. As company agents close in and her own brother is exposed as an informant, Hazel must decide which family member takes the last berth on the escape ship downriver. She gives it to her father, keeps her identity by forging a new one, and ends the story staying behind to run the orchard that hides the smuggling route, having learned that history happens wherever someone refuses to look away.
about_author: Yara Zhou is a former maritime archivist who spent three years cataloguing shipping manifests from Central European river trade before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of empires.

chapters.title: Salt in the Lungs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She dives for pearls at dawn to pay down her indenture, establishing her pragmatism and her belief that grand events belong elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet resignation sharpened by pride in her competence.

chapters.title: The Company Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the Meridian office she transcribes manifests and notices a recurring coded entry tied to the Ravensworth name. Her supervisor warns her not to read what she copies. Beat: first unease, curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Wax
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A sealed letter arrives naming her family in a plot to move the deposed archduke's heir out of the Palatinate. She burns half of it but memorizes the rest. Beat: vertigo — history has arrived at her door.

chapters.title: Father's Orchard
chapters.summary: Father's POV. Old Ravensworth tends apple trees that conceal a disused cellar route to the river, revealing he has been a courier for years. Beat: love shadowed by long-held guilt.

chapters.title: Brother of the Company
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Hazel's brother Tomas, desperate to buy out his own indenture, has been feeding information to company agents. He justifies his betrayal as survival. Beat: self-deception curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Archduke's Orphan
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She meets Ilse, the twelve-year-old heir hidden in the orchard cellar, and recognizes her own younger self in the girl's fear. Beat: reluctant tenderness; duty begins to feel personal.

chapters.title: Manifests and Men
chapters.summary: Company agent Brandt's POV. Brandt closes the net, cross-referencing the coded entries, and suspects Tomas is more useful than reliable. Beat: cold professional menace.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Berths
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The escape ship downriver has room for two: Ilse plus one Ravensworth. Hazel confronts her father about the plot and learns the full cost of his years of service. Beat: fury and grief braided together.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Brandt pressures Tomas to deliver Hazel and the girl; Tomas realizes his family will be discarded once he does. Beat: panic beneath bravado.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The child watches Hazel rehearse the escape route through the orchard and begins to trust her. Beat: fragile hope in a small dark space.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Amid festival crowds, Hazel passes forged papers to the ship's captain and nearly loses them to a pickpocket — saved by a stranger, Marek, who asks no questions. Beat: breathless tension, first spark of connection.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. A river pilot with his own reasons to hate the company, Marek agrees to help — but only if Hazel tells him the whole truth. Beat: guarded attraction against mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt offers Hazel her freedom in exchange for delivering Ilse alone. Beat: temptation laid bare — power corrupting through mercy's shape.

chapters.title: The Cellar Council
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The family argues over the last berth: Father insists it go to Tomas; Hazel refuses to reward betrayal. Beat: love against duty tearing the family open.

chapters.title: Tomas Runs
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Terrified, Tomas flees toward Brandt to sell everything — then sees agents executing a captured courier and understands his fate. Beat: horror as the mirror turns.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An early frost threatens the harvest and the timetable; the ship can wait only two nights. Hazel and Marek finalize the plan while admitting what they feel. Beat: urgency and tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Locks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. Tomas leads Brandt's men to the orchard, then doubles back to warn them, buying time with his arrest. Beat: redemption purchased too late.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the riverbank, Hazel must choose: she puts Ilse aboard with her father's documents and stays herself, giving the berth to no one — because there was never room for two adults. Beat: sacrifice as authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: What the River Takes
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The ship slips past the locks under gunfire; Marek watches Hazel vanish into the reeds, choosing to turn his boat back for her. Beat: love answering duty's claim.

chapters.title: Ash and Apple Blossom
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Brandt finds the orchard empty except for Hazel, who trades the remaining evidence for her family's freedom and his silence. Beat: power meeting its match in a bargainer with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: A New Name, an Old Tree
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Spring returns; Hazel, freed and renamed on paper, runs the orchard as the new node in the escape route, hiding the next fugitive. Beat: identity chosen, not given.

chapters.title: Letters Downriver
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epistolary close. Letters arrive from Father and Ilse in exile; Tomas, released, comes home to work the trees. Hazel plants a sapling over the old cellar and finally believes history happened to her — and that she answered. Beat: hard-won peace.
